findings.issue: The spec's load-bearing premise — 'код к этому готов по построению ... все запросы перечисляют колонки явно, так что добавленные в PG 19 колонки ничего не ломают' (line 26) — only protects against ADDED columns. It says nothing about columns REMOVED or RENAMED in PG 19 from views pgcenter already selects explicitly. Neither the spec nor the code research establishes that no such removal exists: code-research §2.4 enumerates only the four new progress columns, §7.1 audits version-comparison operators, §7.2 audits the one known rename (wait-event type BUFFERPIN → BUFFER). No one enumerated dropped/renamed columns across the ~25 query constants in internal/query/. This exact class of change already happened one version earlier — PG 18 removed columns from pg_stat_wal, which is why SelectStatWALQuery branches at PostgresV18 (architecture.md:65).
findings.why_matters: If PG 19 dropped or renamed a single column that an existing pgcenter query selects, that query errors at execution (internal/stat/stat.go:322 collectPostgresStat → stats.Error), the screen shows no data on every PG 19 server, and fixing it requires a brand-new version branch plus its 33-site test ripple — work not budgeted anywhere in this spec. Three consequences ride on the unverified assumption at once: the 'hygiene, not fixing' framing in Зачем, the size M estimate, and the anti-rework boundary (a removal in the WAL/tables/replication areas would collide with the [016]–[018] deferral policy). The check is cheap and can be done now — the PG 19 release notes and catalog docs against the column lists in internal/query/*.go — and its answer changes the feature's shape, so it belongs before spec approval, not after.
findings.fix: Before approving: audit the PG 19 catalog/release notes for removed and renamed columns across every stats view pgcenter queries (activity, tables, indexes, functions, databases, wal, bgwriter/checkpointer, stat_io, replication, replication_slots, statements family, the six progress views, archiver-adjacent). Record the result in the spec: either state explicitly 'no column pgcenter selects was removed or renamed in PG 19' with the source, or add the affected queries to scope with their version branches and re-check the declared size. Also correct the wording in Зачем so it claims protection against added columns only.

findings.issue: Acceptance criterion 3 ('Все экраны pgcenter top отрисовываются на живом PG 19 без ошибок и без паник', line 138) is contradicted by the mitigation of risk 5 (line 170): if the verification pass finds a real breakage in an area re-entered by [016]–[018] (WAL, replication, tables), the fix is deferred to those features. Under that policy the feature can be declared done while a screen is knowingly broken on PG 19 — and AC 3, the deliverable the spec calls 'то, что превращает «должно работать» в «проверено»', cannot actually be met.
findings.why_matters: This makes the feature's definition of done depend on unbuilt features. Concretely: [012] closes, the release's central promise ('pgcenter does not break on PG 19') is announced, and a screen stays broken until [016] or [018] lands — with no mechanism in this spec to track that or to hold the release. It also means the anti-rework boundary silently doubles as a defect-deferral policy, which is not what the roadmap wrote it for (roadmap-0.12.0.md:93-96 defers new FEATURES, not repairs).
findings.fix: Reconcile the two. Either (a) restrict the deferral to purely additive PG 19 columns and state that any actual breakage found by the verification pass is fixed inside [012] regardless of area, or (b) keep the deferral and rewrite AC 3 to name its escape hatch explicitly — e.g. 'every screen renders without errors, except breakages recorded as blocking items on [016]/[018], each of which must be listed in the spec's Post-implementation section and be a release blocker for 0.12.0'.

findings.issue: The spec spends a dedicated risk entry (line 168), a dedicated acceptance criterion (line 137) and a QA step (line 204) defending against one footgun: internal/postgres/testing.go:35-37 falls back to ports[140000] for an unmapped version, so a forgotten port entry makes every 'PG 19' subtest silently pass against PG 14. The chosen mitigation is a one-time manual ritual — stop the 21919 cluster, run make test, confirm subtests skip. The structural alternative is three lines: make NewTestConnectVersion return an error for an unmapped version instead of falling back.
findings.why_matters: The manual check protects this feature once and is never repeated: PG 20 will reintroduce the identical failure mode, and nothing in patterns.md's 'Adding a New PostgreSQL Version' checklist would catch it. Removing the fallback makes the whole class impossible forever and deletes a risk, an AC and a QA step from this spec. The objection raised in code-research §7.3 — that it would change behaviour for EOL versions — does not hold: PG 9.4–13 are present in the map (testing.go:26-31) and already fail at connect time, which every caller handles with t.Skipf. Only unmapped keys are affected, and there are none today.
findings.fix: Add the fallback removal to scope as a one-line-plus-tests item, or state explicitly in Технические решения why the manual check was preferred over the structural fix. If it stays out of scope, register it as a debt item alongside the pgdg-testing repo entry so the next PG version does not rediscover it.

findings.issue: The user-spec carries implementation detail that belongs in the tech-spec. Specific instances: the constant name and its file (`PostgresV19 = 190000` в `internal/query/query.go`, line 14); the selector-shape decision 'сделать все три селектора одинаковой формы, даже там, где диапазон разностных колонок не меняется, чтобы соседние функции одного семейства не отличались сигнатурами' (line 179); the DiffIntvl mechanics ('диапазон разностных колонок становится версионно-зависимым', lines 122, 177); the RIGHT JOIN internals used as UX justification (line 112); and 'версионные селекторы написаны через неравенства (`version >= PostgresV18`)' (line 26). The selector-arity decision is the clearest case — it has zero user-visible or maintainer-visible consequence and is a pure code-shape choice.
findings.why_matters: User-spec defines WHAT and WHY; HOW belongs in the tech-spec. Freezing function signatures at user-spec time removes the tech-spec's ability to choose the right shape after reading the code, and pre-empts the [007] ADR check (does UniqueKey move? here it does not — code-research §2.5) that should be performed at tech-spec time rather than assumed. It also makes the spec harder for a non-implementer to review: the reader has to hold internal/query package structure in their head to follow the argument.
findings.fix: Move to the tech-spec: the selector-arity uniformity decision (line 179), the constant name/file (keep the user-facing fact 'pgcenter recognises server version 190000'), the DiffIntvl wording (restate as the user-visible consequence: 'the per-interval columns must stay per-interval on PG 19, in both top and report'), and the RIGHT JOIN detail (restate as 'a vacuum row can appear before progress data exists — those cells render blank'). Keep the infrastructure specifics (port 21919, image tag 0.0.11, pgdg-testing, CI tag bump) — the maintainer is a declared user of this feature and those are the deliverable, not the how.

findings.issue: The whole PG 19 code path is developed and validated against beta 1 only, and the spec declares the RC/GA re-verification explicitly non-blocking: 'она не блокирует релиз и не переоткрывает фичу' (line 151). The exposure is described as small because queries list columns explicitly — but that argument does not apply to the three NEW columns, which are the only place where the spec introduces column names read from a beta catalog. There is no stated remedy if GA moves them.
findings.why_matters: If `started_by`, `mode` or `backup_type` is renamed or reshaped between beta 1 and GA, the PG 19 branch of the affected progress query errors on execution and the screen shows no data for every PG 19 user — a hard failure, not a cosmetic drift (a missing column aborts the whole query; the app survives via stats.Error but the screen is unusable). Given PG 19 GA is expected September/October 2026 and 0.12.0 may ship earlier, the release could carry a screen that is broken on the version the release is named after, with no committed timeline for a fix.
findings.fix: Add the remedy path to Ограничения: state that a GA catalog divergence affecting the three new columns triggers a 0.12.x patch release, and/or that the 0.12.0 release notes will state PG 19 support was validated against beta N. Optionally scope the check tighter — if 0.12.0 ships after PG 19 RC, make the re-verification a release blocker for the PG 19 query branches specifically (not for the whole release).

findings.issue: Frontmatter declares `size: M` as settled, while the spec itself makes the size conditional on an unresolved probe: branch 2 of the ladder (line 154) folds a full ubuntu:22.04 → ubuntu:24.04 base-image migration into the feature — recreating the test environment for all of PG 14–18 immediately before a release — and says 'объём фичи пересматривается на этапе tech-spec'. Branch 3 pauses the feature entirely.
findings.why_matters: An approved size is what downstream planning (decomposition, wave count, review budget) is calibrated against. Approving M when the spec itself says the size is unknown until the probe runs means the decomposition either happens against a stale number or has to be redone. The project's own metrics show this matters: [008] at size M was 11 tasks / 4 waves / 18 commits.
findings.fix: Either run the probe before spec approval and fix the size against the result, or mark the frontmatter conditionally (e.g. `size: M` with an explicit note 'M under probe outcome 1; re-declared at tech-spec time under outcome 2') so the number is not read as settled.

findings.issue: The decision to give SelectStatProgressAnalyzeQuery a 3-tuple signature (line 179) makes it return a DiffIntvl of [2]int{0,0} that is identical on both branches and can never vary — a returned value with no purpose, added purely for signature symmetry with its two siblings. The project has established precedent for the 2-tuple in exactly this situation (SelectStatActivityQuery, SelectStatReplicationQuery; patterns.md:24-25 states that when the count is constant, Configure() swaps QueryTmpl alone).
findings.why_matters: It is small, but it is a case of consistency-for-its-own-sake outweighing a documented project pattern, and it adds a Configure() assignment plus test assertions for a value that is constant by construction. It also sets a precedent that future selectors must be 3-tuples regardless of need.
findings.fix: Not blocking — but move the decision to the tech-spec (see the implementation-detail finding) and, if kept, record the trade-off honestly: symmetry chosen over patterns.md's stated rule, cost is one dead return value in two branches.

findings.issue: The edge cases cover backward compatibility (pre-0.12 archive replayed by a 0.12 binary, line 129) but not forward compatibility: an archive recorded by 0.12.0 against PG 19 and replayed by a pre-0.12 pgcenter. The old binary's static view holds DiffIntvl {10,11} / {9,9} and no version selector for the progress views, so it would diff the wrong column pair on the 15/12-column PG 19 layout — producing plausible-looking nonsense with no error, the exact failure mode risk 4 (line 169) names for the other direction.
findings.why_matters: Archives are shared artifacts — recorded on one machine, analysed on another, often with an older binary installed. The failure is silent and the output looks valid. It cannot be fixed in old binaries, but it can be named so it reaches the release notes instead of being discovered by a DBA reading wrong percentages during an incident.
findings.fix: Add an edge case: 'Archive recorded on PG 19 by 0.12.0 and replayed by a pre-0.12 binary — the older binary has no PG 19 layout and will diff the wrong columns silently. Not fixable retroactively; goes in the 0.12.0 release notes as a known limitation.'

summary: A well-argued, well-scoped spec whose plan is sound — but it rests on an unverified premise: nobody checked whether PG 19 removed or renamed any column that pgcenter's existing queries select explicitly, and that answer determines the feature's size, its 'hygiene not fixing' framing, and whether the anti-rework boundary holds. Secondary issues: AC 3 conflicts with the policy of deferring PG 19 breakages to [016]–[018], the silent PG-14 test-connection fallback is defended by a one-time manual check rather than a three-line structural fix, and several tech-spec-level implementation decisions are frozen here.
